description: Per-function gas budgets. Budget values are regression-prevention ceilings (current actual Max + small buffer). Aspirational targets that are tighter live in contracts/README.md §Gas targets and are tracked as future optimisation work. CI fails if any function's Max exceeds its budget here.

deployment.note: Single-shot deployment cost. Upper bound with ~5% headroom.

canSpend.note: view. Called on every sponsor preflight.

createBudget.note: One-time per-agent setup. Aspirational target in README is tighter; follow-up optimisation tracked.

grantSession.note: Called once per session key rotation.

revokeSession.note: Atomic-revocation property path. Aspirational target in README is tighter.

spend.note: Hot path. Aspirational 60k is warm-path with ERC-20 allowance already set + window anchored; current Max is cold-window first-spend.

deployment.note: Pure-storage contract. Deployment cost is well under 1M gas.

anchor.note: Per-batch anchor cost. Budget covers 256-fuzz worst case; aspirational target in README is optimistic.

getBatch.note: view. Used by verifiers cross-checking inclusion proofs.

notes: Regression-prevention: CI fails if any function's Max gas exceeds its budget here.
Aspirational targets in contracts/README.md §Gas targets are tracked as follow-up optimisation work.
When a legitimate optimisation lands, bump currentMax DOWN in the commit that regenerates this file via `forge test --gas-report` → regenerate.
When a feature intentionally adds gas (e.g. new branch), bump the budget UP in the SAME commit that adds the feature — never retroactively.
